vocabulary.definition: This means "I haven't done something yet". the future though. It is part of your plan. It implies that you will do it in "I've yet to start reading that but I will though"

your plan. If you "follow through" on something, it means that you actually do Many people make plans, but they don't follow what is on their plan. If you do what you say you will do or you do what you are planning on doing, you "follow through". "I've been wanting to improve my diet for a long time but I haven't really followed through."

Your "urges" are your instinctual wants or impulses. They could be eating chocolate, playing around on the internet, punching someone when you are angry. You don't have to act on your urges. If you just talk about someone's "urges" with no context, you are often talking about their sexual urges. You might hear something stupid like, "you know, men have urges"

"Gratification" is about a good or positive experience. of course means "immediately". "Instant" "Instant gratification" sounds like it might be a positive term, but it's not. It refers to doing something that is fun or useful in the short term, but bad or unhealthy in the long term. Eating chocolate, pizza, or ice cream, wasting time watching TV, smoking cigarettes, etc, are examples of "instant gratification". Studying English is an example of "delayed gratification". It has long term benefits. course, the 232 is a strange example because using it provides both instant AND delayed gratifacation.
A "front" is the way someone acts or pretends to be. It could be positive or negative, usually negative.

It is fake in some way. "She always acts like she is so sweet and friendly around new people, but it's all a front. She's a huge bitch once you get to know her." "Trust me, he's really sad because his girlfriend left him. He seemed happy yesterday, but it was all a front."

If you are "left to your own devices" it means you are just alone, with no outside help, and doing whatever is natural for you. He works really hard when he has a boss and is working in a company, but when he's left to his own devices, he's super lazy. I go to the gym a lot if I have a friend who motivates me to go with him, but if I'm left to my own devices, I just watch TV and order pizza pretty much every day.
"Scarfing down" food means eating really fast. It's usually, but not always, junk food. I scarfed down that extra large pizza in about 10 minutes.

"Re runs" are TV shows that have already been shown on TV before. They are the old episodes. Usually if a person is watching re runs on TV, they are being lazy and not only watching shows that have been played before, but also watching episodes that you have already seen, perhaps many times!
If something is "mediocre" it means it's not very good. It's just ok. That movie was pretty mediocre. I wouldn't say he's a great tennis player, but he's certainly mediocre.

If something isn't a "pretty picture" it means it's not a good situation. It could be a horrible situation. My favorite basketball team has lost 5 games in a row and their second best player just got injured. It's not a pretty picture. All of the parents who lost their children in the school shooting are going through an incredibly difficult time in their lives right now. It's not a pretty picture.
